authors: O’Hagan, A.; Coleman, G.; O’Connor, R. V.
title: What Empirically Based Research Tells Us About Game Development
notes: Open access systematic review of 48 empirical papers (2006–2016); finds detailed planning difficult under soft requirements and cautions that Agile is often an imprecise label.

authors: Karlsson, T.; Brusk, J.; Engström, H.
title: Level Design Processes and Challenges: A Cross Section of Game Development
notes: Field study and interviews at professional studios; documents interdisciplinary level design, late narrative, and creativity/coordination challenges.

title: Construction trial of a practical education curriculum for game development by industry–university collaboration in Japan
notes: Japanese industry-university curriculum trial; three short production cycles and PDCA in one semester. Educational setting, not representative evidence for all commercial studios.

title: Game development software engineering process life cycle: a systematic review
publication: Journal of Software Engineering Research and Development, 4
notes: Systematic review comparing GDSE life-cycle models and agile approaches.

title: Developers’ Perspectives on Iteration in Game Development
notes: Interview study of 28 developers over two interview waves; reports iteration as essential but practices differ.

title: Database Production: Planners and Players in a Japanese Mobile Game Studio
notes: Six-month ethnographic fieldwork (2012–2013) at a Japanese mobile studio; planners, world construction, and player response.

authors: Viudes-Carbonell, S. J.; Gallego-Durán, F. J.; Llorens-Largo, F.; Molina-Carmona, R.
title: Towards an Iterative Design for Serious Games
notes: Proposes short design-test-evaluate-redesign cycles; serious-games domain, transfer cautiously.

title: Game development life cycle guidelines
notes: GDLC model: initiation, pre-production, production, testing, beta, release; multiple iterations emphasized.

title: Agile development in the video game industry: Examining the effects of iteration and methods of limiting it
notes: Qualitative thesis arguing iteration can have cost and wellbeing downsides; use as a critical perspective, not consensus.

title: Game Design and Emergent Storytelling: The Construction of New Narrative Models in early Japanese videogames
notes: Historical/narrative framing; not a production-process study.

title: FFXIVにおけるシナリオ制作の歩み ～10周年の覚え書き～
notes: First-party session description on long-running live-service scenario production, team evolution, tools, world-setting supervision, writing, direction and resource orders.

title: 至高のシナリオチームの作り方：ライターズルームとシナリオ横串チーム
notes: Primary session description on writers’ room, remote workflows, cross-project scenario management and conflict resolution.

title: ゲーム開発の流れ
notes: Company-published process from research and concept approval through production, concept checks, QA, retrospectives, and live-service analytics/operations.

title: 大規模言語モデルを活用したゲーム内会話パートのスクリプト作成支援への取り組み
notes: Industry case on LLM-assisted script/scene staging element assignment. Treat as tool case, not proof of general quality gains.

title: 現場を理解して実現！ゲーム開発を効率化するWebサービスの開発と、利用促進のための継続的な改善
notes: Internal shared services, scenario/localization tooling, adoption strategy and continuous improvement.

title: 『ヘブンバーンズレッド』のゲームデザイン――ADV、フィールド、バトルパートの全てにおいて「切なさ」を演出
notes: Case report: progress chart coordinates story, implementation, assets, direction, revisions, QA, and external co-development with Key.

authors: 電ファミニコゲーマー編集部
title: 「スマホゲームのシナリオ」は、どう作られている？ 大手のシナリオディレクターに聞く
notes: Practitioner interviews on mobile game scenario production; journalism, not peer-reviewed evidence.

authors: 電ファミニコゲーマー編集部
title: ゲームシナリオ制作会社のリアルな実情
notes: Scenario contractors discuss team organization, external writing and coordination; retrospective practitioner accounts.

title: シナリオプランナー編
notes: First-party role description: quest and text, world-setting, scenario, and wider game-structure responsibilities.

authors: 文化庁メディア芸術カレントコンテンツ
title: 日本のゲーム文化を加速する「国産インディーゲーム」の潮流：インキュベーションプログラム
notes: Japanese indie ecosystem and incubation; includes vertical-slice and mentoring context.

title: インディーゲームの企画・開発・販売を語るプロデューサー座談会
notes: Practitioner discussion on indie development and production constraints; qualitative, non-peer-reviewed.

title: Video Game Development as Public History: Practical Reflections on Making a Video Game for Historical Public Engagement
notes: History-focused game production reflection and ADDIE framing; useful for historical research, interpretive accuracy and evaluation, but not Japan-specific.

title: Noita: A Long Journey of a Game Idea
notes: Longitudinal case method using devlogs, prototypes, builds, interviews and community artifacts; methodological inspiration for postmortem documentation.
